# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server"
```

## Types

### type AccessController

```go
type AccessController interface {
	CheckRead(ctx context.Context, session *Session, nodeID *ua.NodeID) ua.StatusCode
	CheckWrite(ctx context.Context, session *Session, nodeID *ua.NodeID) ua.StatusCode
	CheckBrowse(ctx context.Context, session *Session, nodeID *ua.NodeID) ua.StatusCode
	CheckCall(ctx context.Context, session *Session, methodID *ua.NodeID) ua.StatusCode
}
```

AccessController defines the interface for controlling access to server operations.

Each method is called before the corresponding service executes. Return [ua.StatusOK](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusOK) to allow the operation, or an appropriate status code (e.g., [ua.StatusBadUserAccessDenied](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusBadUserAccessDenied)) to deny it.

The [Session](#type-session) parameter is the session of the request (nil without one): its SessionId, user identity and roles, for role-based or user-based access control.

Provide a custom implementation via [WithAccessController](#func-withaccesscontroller). The default is [DefaultAccessController](#type-defaultaccesscontroller) which allows all operations.

### type CertificateAlarms

```go
type CertificateAlarms struct {
	// ExpirationLimit is how long before the expiry the CertificateExpired
	// alarm becomes active (zero: two weeks, the default of Part 12).
	ExpirationLimit time.Duration
	// CheckInterval is how often the server evaluates the alarms (zero:
	// one minute). They are also evaluated whenever a certificate or a
	// trust list changes.
	CheckInterval time.Duration
}
```

CertificateAlarms configures the alarms of the certificate groups (Part 12 §7.8.3): CertificateExpired (CertificateExpirationAlarmType, Part 12 §7.8.5) of the DefaultApplicationGroup and the DefaultHttpsGroup, active from ExpirationLimit before the certificate of the group that expires first until it is replaced, and TrustListOutOfDate (TrustListOutOfDateAlarmType, Part 12 §7.8.6) of every group, active when the trust list has not been updated for TrustListUpdateFrequency.

The alarms are Alarms & Conditions conditions (Server.AddCondition) with the source node of their certificate group, in the namespace CertificateAlarmsNamespaceURI. They report their events to the group and the Server object.

CertificateStore persists the changes push certificate management makes, so that a restarted server can be configured with them. ApplyChanges calls it before the changes take effect; an error fails ApplyChanges with Bad\_InternalError and keeps the changes pending.

### type ClientCertificateValidator

```go
type ClientCertificateValidator func(certDER []byte) error
```

ClientCertificateValidator validates the application certificate presented by a connecting client during OpenSecureChannel (and again at CreateSession as defense-in-depth). The certificate is provided as DER-encoded bytes.

Return nil to accept the client, or a ua.StatusCode error to reject it. ua.StatusBadCertificateUntrusted is the appropriate code when the certificate is not in the server's configured trust store.

When no validator is registered, the server accepts any application certificate (the secure channel still enforces message security; this validator controls trust-store based application-level access control).

### type Clock

```go
type Clock interface {
	// Now returns the current time.
	Now() time.Time
	// AfterFunc calls f after d (in a goroutine of its own, or, for a
	// test clock, when the test advances the clock). stop prevents the
	// call if it has not happened yet and reports whether it did.
	AfterFunc(d time.Duration, f func()) (stop func() bool)
}
```

Clock is the time source of the alarm timers: shelving, OnDelay / OffDelay, ReAlarmTime and the alarm metrics. The default is the system clock; a test passes its own with [WithAlarmClock](#func-withalarmclock) to run the timers without waiting.

#### func (Condition) EvaluateLimits

```go
func (c *Condition) EvaluateLimits(v float64) error
```

EvaluateLimits compares v with the configured limits of a limit alarm and sets its limit states: an exclusive alarm takes the most severe limit exceeded, a non-exclusive alarm every limit exceeded. A high limit is exceeded when v >= limit, a low limit when v \<= limit.

### type ConditionConfig

```go
type ConditionConfig struct {
	// Type is the ObjectType of the condition: ConditionType or a subtype
	// of it. Default: AlarmConditionType.
	Type *ua.NodeID
	// NodeID is the NodeId of the condition (the ConditionId). Default: a
	// new numeric NodeId in Namespace.
	NodeID *ua.NodeID
	// Namespace receives the nodes of the condition. Default: the namespace
	// of NodeID, else of Source (which must then be a NodeNameSpace other
	// than namespace 0).
	Namespace *NodeNameSpace
	// Name is the BrowseName and the ConditionName (Part 9 §5.5.2).
	Name string
	// Source is the SourceNode of the condition's events: the object or
	// variable the condition is about. It gets a HasCondition and a
	// HasComponent reference to the condition and becomes an event
	// notifier. Required.
	Source *ua.NodeID
	// SourceName is reported in the events. Default: the BrowseName of
	// Source.
	SourceName string
	// Notifiers are further event notifiers that report the events of the
	// condition, in addition to Source and the Server object.
	Notifiers []*ua.NodeID
	// ConditionClassID / ConditionClassName classify the condition.
	// Default: BaseConditionClassType.
	ConditionClassID   *ua.NodeID
	ConditionClassName string
	// Severity and Message are the initial values (1..1000; 0 means 500).
	Severity uint16
	Message  string
	// Retain is the initial Retain of a ConditionType instance. For the
	// acknowledgeable types the server derives Retain from the state.
	Retain bool
	// Disabled creates the condition in the Disabled state.
	Disabled bool
	// Confirmable adds the optional ConfirmedState and the Confirm method
	// (acknowledgeable types).
	Confirmable bool
	// Suppressible adds the optional SuppressedState (alarm types).
	Suppressible bool
	// Shelving adds the ShelvingState with the TimedShelve, OneShotShelve
	// and Unshelve methods (alarm types). MaxTimeShelved, when set, bounds
	// the shelving time and is exposed as the MaxTimeShelved Property.
	Shelving       bool
	MaxTimeShelved time.Duration
	// Serviceable adds the optional OutOfServiceState with the
	// RemoveFromService(2) and PlaceInService(2) methods (alarm types).
	Serviceable bool
	// Silenceable adds the optional SilenceState with the Silence method
	// (alarm types). A new activation of the alarm ends the silence.
	Silenceable bool
	// Latching adds the optional LatchedState with the Reset(2) methods
	// (alarm types): the alarm latches when it becomes active and stays
	// latched (and retained) until it is inactive and reset.
	Latching bool
	// Branching keeps the previous occurrence of an alarm that becomes
	// active again before its last activation was acknowledged (and
	// confirmed): the server moves that state to a branch with its own
	// BranchId, which a client acknowledges and confirms with the EventId
	// of the branch (Part 9 §5.5.2, §4.4). Acknowledgeable types.
	Branching bool
	// Dialog makes the condition a dialog (DialogConditionType and its
	// subtypes, Part 9 §5.6); required for those types.
	Dialog *DialogConfig
	// SuppressionGroups are AlarmSuppressionGroups (see
	// [Server.AddAlarmGroup]) whose suppression suppresses the alarm; it
	// needs Suppressible.
	SuppressionGroups []*ua.NodeID
	// AudibleSound adds the AudibleEnabled Property and the AudibleSound
	// variable (AudioVariableType) of an alarm (Part 9 §5.8.2): the sound
	// a console plays for it. AudibleEnabled starts true;
	// ConditionUpdate.AudibleEnabled changes it.
	AudibleSound *AudibleSound
	// OnDelay adds the OnDelay Property of an alarm: an activation is
	// reported only when the alarm stays active for OnDelay; one that ends
	// earlier is never reported. OffDelay adds the OffDelay Property: the
	// alarm stays active for OffDelay after it returns to normal, and an
	// activation within that time continues the alarm without a new
	// occurrence (Part 9 §5.8.2). The delays apply to the changes of
	// ActiveState (Active, Limit and NonExclusiveLimits of an update);
	// the other changes of the update take effect at once.
	OnDelay, OffDelay time.Duration
	// ReAlarmTime adds the ReAlarmTime Property and the ReAlarmRepeatCount
	// variable of an alarm: an alarm that is still active ReAlarmTime after
	// its activation (or its last re-alarm) is reported again as if it had
	// just become active (unacknowledged, unconfirmed, not silenced), and
	// ReAlarmRepeatCount counts the re-alarms of the activation.
	ReAlarmTime time.Duration
	// FirstInGroup is an alarm group (see [Server.AddAlarmGroup]) whose
	// first-out alarm the alarm can be: it adds the FirstInGroupFlag
	// variable and the FirstInGroup object (AlarmGroupType, listing the
	// alarms with the same FirstInGroup) and makes the alarm a member of
	// the group. FirstInGroupFlag is true for the alarm that became active
	// first while none of these alarms was active, until all of them are
	// inactive again.
	FirstInGroup *ua.NodeID
	// InputNode is the InputNode Property of an alarm.
	InputNode *ua.NodeID
	// NormalState is the NormalState Property of an OffNormalAlarmType.
	NormalState *ua.NodeID
	// Limits are the limits of a LimitAlarmType (and subtypes).
	Limits AlarmLimits
	// Properties are further Properties of the condition, such as those
	// of a subtype of the types above (ExpirationDate of
	// CertificateExpirationAlarmType). They are nodes of the instance and
	// fields of its events.
	Properties []ConditionProperty

	// The hooks are called when a client calls the method, after the
	// checks of the state (a call the state machine refuses does not reach
	// them) and before the change is made; a status other than Good
	// refuses the call with that status. They run without locks held, so
	// they may read or change the condition.
	OnAcknowledge func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnConfirm     func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnAddComment  func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnEnable      func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, enable bool) ua.StatusCode
	OnShelve      func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, state ShelvingState, shelvingTime time.Duration) ua.StatusCode
	// The hooks of the Part 9 1.05 methods; comment is nil for the
	// variants without a Comment argument.
	OnSuppress func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, suppress bool, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnService  func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, inService bool, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnSilence  func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition) ua.StatusCode
	OnReset    func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
	OnRespond  func(ctx context.Context, c *Condition, selectedResponse int32, comment *ua.LocalizedText) ua.StatusCode
}
```

ConditionConfig describes a condition instance for [Server.AddCondition](#func-server-addcondition).

### type ConditionUpdate

```go
type ConditionUpdate struct {
	// Active sets the ActiveState of an alarm. Becoming active makes the
	// alarm unacknowledged and unconfirmed again (Part 9 §5.8.2); becoming
	// inactive ends a OneShotShelved state.

	// Severity sets the Severity; LastSeverity takes the previous value.

	// Message sets the Message of the event.

	Retain *bool
	// Acked / Confirmed set the AckedState / ConfirmedState directly, e.g.
	// to require a new acknowledgement of a non-alarm condition.

	Confirmed *bool
	// Suppressed sets the SuppressedState of an alarm.

	// Limit sets the active limit of an exclusive limit alarm; ActiveState
	// follows (active unless LimitNone).
	Limit *LimitState
	// NonExclusiveLimits sets the limit states of a non-exclusive limit

	NonExclusiveLimits *NonExclusiveLimits

	// SilenceState and LatchedState of an alarm that has them.

	// DialogActive shows (true) or withdraws (false) a dialog; Prompt sets
	// its Prompt.

	// AudibleEnabled sets the AudibleEnabled of an alarm with AudibleSound.
```

```go
type EventHistoryOptions struct {

	// A client that reads a field the filter does not select gets
```

### type EventHistoryProvider

```go
type EventHistoryProvider interface {
	// RecordEvent stores an event reported on notifier. A notifier the
	// provider keeps no history for ignores it. The provider owns ev
	// afterwards; the server does not change it.
	RecordEvent(notifier *ua.NodeID, ev *HistoricalEvent)

	// ReadEvents returns the events of notifier whose Time lies in the
	// range of startTime and endTime (Part 11 §6.5.2.2: oldest first, or
	// newest first when startTime is after endTime or only endTime is
	// given) and that match, at most numValues of them (0: no limit), and a
	// continuation point when more events match. A continued read passes
	// the continuation point and the same arguments. The status is Good,
	// Good_NoData without events, Bad_HistoryOperationUnsupported for a
	// notifier without event history and Bad_ContinuationPointInvalid for
	// an unknown continuation point. match is called without locks of the
	// provider held.
	ReadEvents(notifier *ua.NodeID, startTime, endTime time.Time, numValues uint32, match func(*HistoricalEvent) bool, continuationPoint []byte) ([]*HistoricalEvent, []byte, ua.StatusCode)
}
```

EventHistoryProvider optionally keeps the event history of notifiers (HistoricalEventNodes, Part 11 §5.4) and serves HistoryRead ReadEventDetails (Part 11 §6.5.2). The server hands it every event reported on a notifier whose EventNotifier attribute has the HistoryRead bit (Part 3 §5.4, Part 11 §5.4.4), and releases its continuation points through [HistoryProvider.ReleaseContinuation](#func-historyprovider-releasecontinuation).

### type EventHistoryUpdater

```go
type EventHistoryUpdater interface {
	UpdateEvents(notifier *ua.NodeID, perform ua.PerformUpdateType, events []*HistoricalEvent) *ua.HistoryUpdateResult
}
```

EventHistoryUpdater optionally supports HistoryUpdate UpdateEventDetails (Part 11 §6.9.4). The server validates the details and builds the events: each has an EventId, and those to insert have an EventType and a Time.

Semantics, per event (OperationResults):

  - Insert: Bad\_EntryExists when an event with the EventId exists; else insert, Good\_EntryInserted
  - Replace: Bad\_NoEntryExists when no event has the EventId; else replace the event, Good\_EntryReplaced
  - Update: replace when an event has the EventId (Good\_EntryReplaced), else insert (Good\_EntryInserted)

### type Historian

```go
type Historian struct {

	// keyed by NodeID.String()

	// continuations stores active continuation points.

	// modifications records HistoryUpdate changes for ReadModified.

	// events holds the event history per notifier (EnableEvents), keyed by
	// NodeID.String(); eventCPs the continuation points of event reads.

	// eventSeq orders the stored events of the same Time.

}
```

Historian is the default in-memory HistoryProvider.

Retention is bounded: each EnableNode call sets a per-node ring buffer (default 1000 samples), each EnableEvents call one of events per notifier (default 1000 events). Storage is not durable across process restarts. Continuation points expire after 30s and are capped at 100 active tokens.

```go

```

ReadEvents implements EventHistoryProvider.

The range (Part 11 §6.5.2.2): with startTime before endTime the events from startTime (inclusive) to endTime (exclusive), oldest first; with startTime after endTime the events from startTime (inclusive) back to endTime (exclusive), newest first; with equal times the events of that Time. With only startTime the events from startTime on, oldest first; with only endTime the events up to endTime (inclusive), newest first.

### type HistoricalEvent

```go
type HistoricalEvent struct {
	Fields map[string]*ua.Variant
}
```

HistoricalEvent is an event in the event history of a notifier. Fields holds its fields by their BrowsePath, the names joined with "/" ("EventId", "Time", "AckedState/Id"); the key "" holds the ConditionId of a condition event (the SelectClause with an empty BrowsePath and AttributeId NodeId, Part 9 §5.5.2). A field that is not there is null. Providers treat a HistoricalEvent as immutable.

### type IssuedTokenValidator

```go
type IssuedTokenValidator func(tok *ua.IssuedIdentityToken) error
```

IssuedTokenValidator validates an IssuedIdentityToken (a JWT, a Kerberos ticket or another token from an authorization service) presented by a client during ActivateSession. TokenData holds the token as the issuer created it: the server has already decrypted it where the security policy encrypts it.

Return nil to accept the token, or an error to reject it (ua.StatusBadIdentityTokenRejected or ua.StatusBadUserAccessDenied).


LDSAllowInsecureRegistration accepts RegisterServer and RegisterServer2 on SecureChannels without security (SecurityPolicy None). Anybody who can reach the discovery server can then register, replace and remove servers. It is meant for tests and closed lab networks.

#### func LDSApplicationType

```go
func LDSApplicationType(t ua.ApplicationType) LDSOption
```

LDSApplicationType sets the ApplicationType the server reports about itself. A discovery server that offers nothing else should use ua.ApplicationTypeDiscoveryServer; the default is ua.ApplicationTypeServer.

#### func LDSMaxRegisteredServers

```go
func LDSMaxRegisteredServers(n int) LDSOption
```

LDSMaxRegisteredServers bounds the number of registrations (1024 by default). Further servers are refused with BadResourceUnavailable.

#### func LDSRegistrationCallback

```go
func LDSRegistrationCallback(fn func(server *ua.RegisteredServer)) LDSOption
```

LDSRegistrationCallback sets a function that is called for every accepted RegisterServer and RegisterServer2 request, registrations (IsOnline true, renewals included) and unregistrations alike. The argument is a copy. The function is called from the request handling goroutine and must not block.

#### func LDSRegistrationTimeout

```go
func LDSRegistrationTimeout(d time.Duration) LDSOption
```

LDSRegistrationTimeout sets how long a registration lives without being renewed. Zero or a negative value disables the expiry: registrations then only end by unregistering or through their semaphore file.

#### func LDSSkipServerURICheck

```go
func LDSSkipServerURICheck() LDSOption
```

LDSSkipServerURICheck accepts a registration on a secured channel whose ServerUri is not the application URI of the certificate the channel was opened with. Without it an application can only register (and unregister) itself.

### type MapNamespace

```go
type MapNamespace struct {
```

MapNamespace provides a convenient way to have data mapped to the OPC server without having to map your application data to the OPC-UA data abstraction.

```go
type MethodCaller struct {

	// SecurityPolicyURI and SecurityMode are those of the secure channel.

	// Identity is the user identity token of the session, without the

	// AuditEntryID is the AuditEntryId of the request header (Part 4

	// ClientCertificate is the application instance certificate (DER, the

	// handshake proved that the client holds its key.
```

### type NameSpace

```go
type NameSpace interface {
	// Name of the namespace.  Per the standard it should be an URI.
	Name() string

	// This function should create a new node
	AddNode(n *Node) *Node

	// DeleteNode removes the node with the given ID from the namespace.
	// Returns StatusBadNodeIDUnknown if the node does not exist.
	DeleteNode(id *ua.NodeID) ua.StatusCode

	// This function should lookup and return the node indicated by the Node ID
	Node(id *ua.NodeID) *Node

	// This function should return the base Objects node that contains other nodes
	Objects() *Node

	// This function should return the root node
	Root() *Node

	// This is the function to list all available nodes to the client that is browsing.
	// The BrowseDescription has the root node of the browse and what kind of nodes the
	// client is looking for.  The Browse Result should have the list of matching nodes.
	Browse(req *ua.BrowseDescription) *ua.BrowseResult

	// ID and SetID are the namespace ID number of this namespace.  When you add it to the server
	// with srv.AddNamespace(xxx) it will set these for you.
	ID() uint16
	SetID(uint16)

	// These are the functions for reading and writing arbitrary attributes.  The most common
	// is the value attribute, but many clients also read the datatype and description attributes.
	// as well as attributes related to array bounds
	Attribute(*ua.NodeID, ua.AttributeID) *ua.DataValue
	SetAttribute(*ua.NodeID, ua.AttributeID, *ua.DataValue) ua.StatusCode
}
```

NameSpace defines the interface for an OPC-UA address space partition.

Each namespace manages a set of nodes identified by a shared namespace index. The server dispatches service requests (Browse, Read, Write, etc.) to the appropriate namespace based on the NamespaceIndex in the NodeID.

Two implementations are provided:

  - [NodeNameSpace](#type-nodenamespace): Full OPC-UA node graph with references and type definitions
  - [MapNamespace](#type-mapnamespace): Simple key-value mapping for IoT and sensor data

Custom implementations can be registered with [Server.AddNamespace](#func-server-addnamespace).

#### func NewVariableNode

```go

```

NewVariableNode returns a Variable node with the given name and value, without references.

value is the initial value (any type ua.NewVariant accepts, an int is an Int32, a \*ua.Variant or \*ua.DataValue as is) or a ValueFunc / func() \*ua.DataValue called on every read.

The BrowseName is in the namespace of nodeID. For a value the DataType attribute is the DataType of the value (Part 3 §5.6.2): the built-in type of the Variant (Double, String, ...), the DataType of a structure in namespace 0, Structure for other structures and BaseDataType for nil; ValueRank is Scalar (-1) for a scalar, the number of dimensions for an array (with ArrayDimensions 0, any length) and Any (-2) for nil. For a function the DataType is that of the value it returns, worked out on each read, and the ValueRank Any. Callers that want other attributes set them with SetAttribute, which overrides these.

#### func (Node) AddRef

```go
func (n *Node) AddRef(o *Node, rt RefType, forward bool)
```

AddRef adds a reference of type rt between n and o: n -rt-> o when forward, o -rt-> n otherwise. A Reference has a forward and an inverse direction and Browse returns either (Part 3 §7.1, Part 4 §5.8.2), so both ends record it: n gets the reference to o and o the opposite direction to n. Adding a reference both ends already hold (also from the other end, as parent.AddRef(child, rt, true) followed by child.AddRef(parent, rt, false)) does not add it again.


RemoveRef removes the reference of type refTypeID between n and the node targetID (n -> target when forward, target -> n otherwise) from both ends, as AddRef records it on both. It reports whether either end held it. The other end is found through the server of n's namespace; a node that was not added to a namespace, or a target on another server, loses this end only.

#### func (Node) SetMethodArguments

```go
func (n *Node) SetMethodArguments(in, out []*ua.Argument) error
```

SetMethodArguments gives the Method node n its InputArguments and OutputArguments Properties (Part 3 §5.7): Variables of the PropertyType with the DataType Argument, ValueRank OneDimension and an array of the arguments as value, referenced with HasProperty. Clients read the signature of the method from them (Client.MethodArguments) and the Call service checks the input arguments against InputArguments.

n must be a Method node added to a namespace (with AddNode); the Properties are added to the same namespace. Their NodeIds are string NodeIds in the namespace of n: "\<id>.InputArguments" and "\<id>.OutputArguments", where \<id> is the identifier of a string NodeId and the NodeId without namespace ("i=7001") otherwise. A nil or empty list leaves the Property out, as Part 3 §5.7 asks for a method without input or output arguments; calling SetMethodArguments again replaces the arguments, removing a Property whose list is now empty.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*serverConfig) error
```

Option is an option function type to modify the configuration.

#### func AllowUsernameOnNone

```go
func AllowUsernameOnNone() Option
```

AllowUsernameOnNone permits the server to advertise UserName token policies on None/None (unencrypted) endpoints.  The OPC UA specification permits this for test deployments (Part 4 §5.6.3.2).  By default, non-anonymous tokens are only advertised on encrypted endpoints.

#### func ApplicationIdentity

```go
func ApplicationIdentity(cert []byte, key crypto.Signer) Option
```

ApplicationIdentity adds an application instance certificate and its private key to the server. It may be given several times, once per key type, and combined with Certificate and PrivateKey:

  - an RSA certificate serves the RSA security policies (Basic256Sha256, Aes128\_Sha256\_RsaOaep, Aes256\_Sha256\_RsaPss, ...),
  - an ECDSA P-256 certificate serves ECC\_nistP256, ECC\_nistP256\_AesGcm and ECC\_nistP256\_ChaChaPoly,
  - an ECDSA P-384 certificate serves ECC\_nistP384 and the three ECC\_nistP256 policies,
  - an Ed25519 certificate serves ECC\_curve25519,
  - an ECDSA brainpoolP256r1 certificate serves ECC\_brainpoolP256r1, a brainpoolP384r1 one ECC\_brainpoolP384r1 and ECC\_brainpoolP256r1,
  - an Ed448 certificate serves ECC\_curve448.

A server that offers RSA and ECC endpoints therefore has (at least) two certificates. For every SecureChannel the server uses the first configured certificate whose key fits the security policy the client selected, and each endpoint advertises the certificate of its policy. All certificates of a server should carry the same ApplicationURI.

cert is the DER encoded certificate. An ECC key only has to sign, so it may be any crypto.Signer with an ECDSA, Ed25519 or Ed448 public key (for example a key held in an HSM); an RSA key must be an \*rsa.PrivateKey. Certificates with Brainpool and Ed448 keys are parsed with uapolicy.ParseCertificate.

#### func ApplicationURI

```go
func ApplicationURI(uri string) Option
```

ApplicationURI sets the ApplicationUri of the server: the globally unique name it reports in its endpoint descriptions and announces as ServerUri when it opens a reverse connection (see [WithReverseConnect](#func-withreverseconnect)).

A server with a certificate does not need this option: the ApplicationUri is taken from the certificate (see [Certificate](#func-certificate)), with which it must be identical anyway. Use it for a server without a certificate, which has no ApplicationUri otherwise.

#### func Certificate

```go
func Certificate(cert []byte) Option
```

Certificate sets the client X509 certificate in the secure channel configuration and also detects and sets the ApplicationURI from the URI within the certificate.

#### func EnableAuthMode

```go
func EnableAuthMode(tokenType ua.UserTokenType) Option
```

EnableAuthMode registers a new user authentication mode to the server. All AuthModes except Anonymous require encryption by default, so EnableSecurity() must also be called with at least one non-"None" SecurityPolicy.

The UserName, Certificate and IssuedToken modes also need their validator (WithUsernameValidator, WithX509UserValidator, WithIssuedTokenValidator): without it the server advertises the token type but rejects every token of that type, and New logs a warning.

#### func EnableSecurity

```go
func EnableSecurity(secPolicy string, secMode ua.MessageSecurityMode) Option
```

EnableSecurity registers a new endpoint security mode to the server. This will also register the security policy against each enabled auth mode. Policy None also needs [InsecureNoSecurity](#func-insecurenosecurity).

#### func EnableUAJSON

```go
func EnableUAJSON() Option
```

EnableUAJSON makes the opc.wss and opc.https endpoints serve the UA JSON mappings of their transports as well:

  - https-uajson (Part 6 §7.4.5): an HTTPS request with the Content-Type application/json (or application/opcua+uajson, which UA-.NETStandard sends) is a JSON message (Part 6 §5.4.9), answered by one, and may be gzip compressed. The security policies are those of https-uabinary.
  - wss-uajson (Part 6 §7.5.2): a WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uajson carries one JSON message per WebSocket message, with no HEL/ACK and no secure conversation. Its requests are served concurrently and answered as they complete; a client correlates them by RequestHandle. A WebSocket cannot name a security policy, so it is only offered when None with the mode None is enabled (or no security is configured at all), and TLS alone protects the messages.

The JSON endpoints are advertised next to the binary ones, at the same URLs, with the transport profiles ua.TransportProfileHTTPSJSON and ua.TransportProfileWSSJSON. Responses are written in the compact JSON form; requests may use the compact or the verbose form.

#### func EndPoint

```go
func EndPoint(host string, port int) Option
```

EndPoint adds an advertised endpoint to the server based on the host name and port.  The first EndPoint registered is also used as the TCP bind address unless ListenOn is called explicitly.

host is a host name or an IP address. An IPv6 literal is bracketed in the endpoint URL ("::1" gives opc.tcp://\[::1]:4840) and may be given with or without the brackets; a zone ("fe80::1%eth0") is written as %25 in the URL (RFC 6874) and the server binds to that zone.

#### func HTTPSEndPoint

```go
func HTTPSEndPoint(host string, port int) Option
```

HTTPSEndPoint adds an opc.https endpoint at host and port: UA Binary over HTTPS (Part 6 §7.4, transport profile https-uabinary). Every request is an HTTP POST; there is no secure conversation, TLS protects the messages and the security policy only decides how the session nonces are signed. It offers each enabled security policy that does not need a secure conversation (see uasc.HTTPSPolicySupported) with the modes enabled for it. The server listens on the first HTTPS endpoint unless ListenHTTPSOn says otherwise; port 0 picks a free port. The TLS certificate is set with TLSConfig.

#### func InsecureNoSecurity

```go
func InsecureNoSecurity() Option
```

InsecureNoSecurity offers endpoints without message security: security policy None and security mode None. Messages are neither signed nor encrypted and clients are not authenticated by a certificate.

[Server.Start](#func-server-start) refuses a server that offers None without this option, and a server with no security configured at all (errors.ErrInsecureNotAllowed). A secure-only server still answers the discovery services, which the specification defines without security.

#### func ListenHTTPSOn

```go
func ListenHTTPSOn(addr string) Option
```

ListenHTTPSOn sets the TCP address the HTTPS transport binds to (e.g. "0.0.0.0:4843"), as ListenOn does for opc.tcp.

#### func ListenOn

```go
func ListenOn(addr string) Option
```

ListenOn sets the TCP address the server binds to (e.g. "0.0.0.0:4840"). Use this when you want the server to accept connections on all interfaces without advertising "0.0.0.0" as a reachable endpoint URL.  If not set, the server listens on the first EndPoint address.

#### func ListenWebSocketOn

```go
func ListenWebSocketOn(addr string) Option
```

ListenWebSocketOn sets the TCP address the WebSocket transport binds to (e.g. "0.0.0.0:4843"), as ListenOn does for opc.tcp.

#### func ManufacturerName

```go
func ManufacturerName(name string) Option
```

#### func PrivateKey

```go
func PrivateKey(key *rsa.PrivateKey) Option
```

PrivateKey sets the RSA private key in the secure channel configuration.

Together with Certificate it configures the server's RSA application instance certificate. Certificates of other key types, for the ECC security policies, are added with ApplicationIdentity.

#### func ProductName

```go
func ProductName(name string) Option
```

#### func ServerName

```go
func ServerName(name string) Option
```

#### func SetLogger

```go
func SetLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

SetLogger sets the logger for the server. By default logging is disabled (silent discard handler). Pass nil to restore the silent default.

#### func SoftwareVersion

```go
func SoftwareVersion(name string) Option
```

#### func TLSConfig

```go
func TLSConfig(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

TLSConfig sets the TLS configuration of the opc.wss and opc.https endpoints: the server's TLS certificate (Certificates or GetCertificate) and, to require client TLS certificates, ClientAuth and ClientCAs. The TLS certificate may differ from the application instance certificate (Part 6 §7.5.3); without this option the RSA application instance certificate and its key are used. TLS 1.2 is the minimum version whatever cfg says.

#### func WebSocketEndPoint

```go
func WebSocketEndPoint(host string, port int) Option
```

WebSocketEndPoint adds an opc.wss endpoint at host and port: OPC UA Secure Conversation and UA Binary over a TLS secured WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uacp (Part 6 §7.5, transport profile wss-uasc-uabinary). The server listens for WebSocket connections on the first one, next to the opc.tcp listener, unless ListenWebSocketOn says otherwise. Port 0 picks a free port. All the security policies and modes enabled on the server are offered, as on opc.tcp. The TLS certificate is set with TLSConfig.

#### func WithAccessController

```go
func WithAccessController(ac AccessController) Option
```

WithAccessController sets a custom access controller on the server.

#### func WithAlarmClock

```go
func WithAlarmClock(clock Clock) Option
```

WithAlarmClock sets the clock of the alarm timers (default: the system clock).

#### func WithAuditing

```go
func WithAuditing(enabled bool) Option
```

WithAuditing turns the audit events on or off (default off).

#### func WithClientCertificateTrustList

```go
func WithClientCertificateTrustList(caCertDER ...[]byte) Option
```

WithClientCertificateTrustList configures the server to verify connecting clients' application certificates against the provided CA certificate pool. Clients that present a certificate not signed by one of the provided CA certificates are rejected with BadCertificateUntrusted at OpenSecureChannel (CreateSession retains the same check as defense-in-depth).

Each caCertDER is a DER-encoded X.509 CA certificate (or a trusted self-signed application instance certificate). Brainpool and Ed448 keys are supported; see uapolicy.VerifyCertificate. Passing an empty list configures a server that rejects all client certificates.

#### func WithDiscoveryRegistration

```go
func WithDiscoveryRegistration(discoveryServerURL string, opts ...RegistrationOption) Option
```

WithDiscoveryRegistration registers the server with the discovery server at discoveryServerURL, e.g. the Local Discovery Server of its machine at "opc.tcp://localhost:4840", and keeps the registration alive.

The registration runs in the background from [Server.Start](#func-server-start) on: the server calls RegisterServer2 (with its mDNS server name and capabilities) and falls back to RegisterServer if the discovery server does not know that service; it repeats the call every [RegisterInterval](#func-registerinterval) so that the registration does not expire, and it retries with an exponential back-off while the discovery server cannot be reached. Neither Start nor [Server.Close](#func-server-close) wait for a discovery server that is down. On Close the server unregisters (IsOnline false).

The SecureChannel to the discovery server is secured: the server picks the most secure endpoint the discovery server offers that one of its own certificates fits ([Certificate](#func-certificate) and [PrivateKey](#func-privatekey), or [ApplicationIdentity](#func-applicationidentity) for the ECC policies) and uses that certificate, whose application URI is the ServerUri it registers. See [RegisterSecurity](#func-registersecurity) and [RegisterInsecure](#func-registerinsecure).

The option can be given several times to register with several discovery servers.

#### func WithIssuedTokenValidator

```go
func WithIssuedTokenValidator(v IssuedTokenValidator) Option
```

WithIssuedTokenValidator registers the validator called during ActivateSession when the client presents an IssuedIdentityToken. EnableAuthMode(ua.UserTokenTypeIssuedToken) must also be called.

If no validator is registered the server rejects all issued tokens, as it does X.509 user tokens without an X509UserValidator.

#### func WithLocalDiscoveryServer

```go
func WithLocalDiscoveryServer(opts ...LDSOption) Option
```

WithLocalDiscoveryServer makes the server a Local Discovery Server (LDS, OPC UA Part 12): it accepts RegisterServer and RegisterServer2 and returns the registered servers from FindServers, after itself.

A registration is removed when the server unregisters (IsOnline false), when its semaphore file disappears, or when it has not been renewed within the registration timeout ([LDSRegistrationTimeout](#func-ldsregistrationtimeout), an hour by default).

Registration changes what clients are told about the network, so by default it is only accepted on a SecureChannel with message security (Sign or SignAndEncrypt), from an application whose certificate carries the registered ServerUri. Which certificates may open such a channel is decided by [WithClientCertificateTrustList](#func-withclientcertificatetrustlist). See [LDSAllowInsecureRegistration](#func-ldsallowinsecureregistration) and [LDSSkipServerURICheck](#func-ldsskipserveruricheck) for the lab settings.

Combine it with [WithMulticastDiscovery](#func-withmulticastdiscovery) for the multicast extension (LDS-ME): registered servers are then announced with mDNS.

#### func WithMaxPendingResponses

```go
func WithMaxPendingResponses(n int) Option
```

WithMaxPendingResponses sets how many requests of one secure channel may be in flight, that is received but not yet answered on the wire, at a time.

When a client has n requests in flight the server stops reading further requests from that client until responses have been written. This bounds the memory one client can occupy with queued responses and applies TCP back pressure to a client that sends requests faster than it reads the answers; it never drops a request. Publish requests that are waiting for a notification do not count.

The default is 256. Zero or a negative value selects the default.

#### func WithMaxSessions

```go
func WithMaxSessions(n int) Option
```

WithMaxSessions sets how many sessions the server keeps at a time, activated or not. CreateSession fails with Bad\_TooManySessions when the server has that many (Part 4 §5.6.2); a session that is closed or times out frees its place. The limit is published as ServerCapabilities.MaxSessions (Part 5 §6.3.2).

The default is 100. Zero or a negative value selects the default.

#### func WithMaxSubscriptions

```go
func WithMaxSubscriptions(n int) Option
```

WithMaxSubscriptions sets how many subscriptions the server keeps at a time over all sessions, including those whose session was closed without deleting them and that wait for their lifetime to expire. CreateSubscription fails with Bad\_TooManySubscriptions when the server has that many (Part 4 §5.13.2). The limit is published as ServerCapabilities.MaxSubscriptions (Part 5 §6.3.2).

The default is 1024. Zero or a negative value selects the default.

#### func WithMaxSubscriptionsPerSession

```go
func WithMaxSubscriptionsPerSession(n int) Option
```

WithMaxSubscriptionsPerSession sets how many subscriptions one session may own. CreateSubscription fails with Bad\_TooManySubscriptions when the session has that many (Part 4 §5.13.2), and TransferSubscriptions does not move more subscriptions into a session than that: the excess ones get Bad\_TooManySubscriptions in their TransferResult and stay where they are. The limit is published as ServerCapabilities.MaxSubscriptionsPerSession (Part 5 §6.3.2).

The default is 64. Zero or a negative value selects the default.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m ServerMetrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets a metrics callback handler for the server. All methods are called synchronously; implementations must be non-blocking.

#### func WithMulticastDiscovery

```go
func WithMulticastDiscovery(opts ...MulticastOption) Option
```

WithMulticastDiscovery enables multicast discovery (the multicast extension of OPC UA Part 12, mDNS and DNS-SD): the server announces itself as a "\_opcua-tcp.\_tcp" service on the local network, keeps a table of the OPC UA servers announced by others and returns it from FindServersOnNetwork. A server that is also a Local Discovery Server ([WithLocalDiscoveryServer](#func-withlocaldiscoveryserver)) announces the servers registered with it as well.

The mDNS implementation is built in and needs no system service. It uses UDP port 5353 on every multicast capable interface (see [MulticastInterfaces](#func-multicastinterfaces)) and shares the port with a system responder such as Avahi or Bonjour. [Server.Start](#func-server-start) fails if no interface can be used.

Multicast discovery tells everybody on the local network segment that the server exists, where it is and what it can do, and it trusts what others announce: see docs/security.md.

#### func WithPubSub

```go
func WithPubSub(cfg *ua.PubSubConfigurationDataType, opts ...pubsub.Option) Option
```

WithPubSub makes the server a PubSub publisher and subscriber (Part 14): it runs a PubSub runtime for cfg, started and stopped with the server, and publishes the PublishSubscribe information model below the Server object (i=14443), with the methods that let clients configure it (AddConnection, AddWriterGroup, ...).

cfg may be nil for an empty, enabled runtime that clients configure. The runtime reads published variables from the address space and writes the target variables of readers to it, and the targets of its PublishedActionMethods call the Methods of the address space; opts can replace these sources and add handlers and key sources. The runtime is available with [Server.PubSub](#func-server-pubsub).

#### func WithPubSubAuthorizer

```go
func WithPubSubAuthorizer(a PubSubAuthorizer) Option
```

WithPubSubAuthorizer restricts the PubSub configuration methods. Without it every session may call them, as with open62541.

#### func WithPushManagement

```go
func WithPushManagement(pm PushManagement) Option
```

WithPushManagement enables certificate management by the push model of Part 12 §7. See [PushManagement](#type-pushmanagement).

#### func WithResponseWriteTimeout

```go
func WithResponseWriteTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithResponseWriteTimeout sets how long the server waits for a response to be written to a client before it gives up on that client.

Every secure channel has its own response writer, so a client that stops reading its responses does not hold up the others. Once a response to such a client has been waiting for d, the client is considered stalled and its connection is closed; its session and subscriptions then end through their own timeouts unless the client reconnects. Other channels are not affected.

The default is 15 seconds. Choose a larger value for clients on very slow links that fetch large responses. Zero or a negative value selects the default.

#### func WithReverseConnect

```go
func WithReverseConnect(clientURL string, opts ...ReverseConnectOption) Option
```

WithReverseConnect makes the server open reverse connections to the client listening at clientURL ("opc.tcp://host:port") once it is started. See [Server.AddReverseConnect](#func-server-addreverseconnect) for the details; the handles of the targets configured this way are available from [Server.ReverseConnects](#func-server-reverseconnects).

#### func WithRoleMapper

```go
func WithRoleMapper(rm RoleMapper) Option
```

WithRoleMapper configures a custom role mapper for session identity → role resolution.

#### func WithServerDiagnostics

```go
func WithServerDiagnostics(enabled bool) Option
```

WithServerDiagnostics sets whether the server collects diagnostics from the start: the initial value of Server.ServerDiagnostics.EnabledFlag (Part 5 §6.3.3). The default is true. A client with the SecurityAdmin or ConfigureAdmin role can change it at runtime by writing EnabledFlag.

#### func WithSessionObserver

```go
func WithSessionObserver(o SessionObserver) Option
```

WithSessionObserver sets the observer of client connections and sessions (nil: none). See [SessionObserver](#type-sessionobserver).

#### func WithSlogLogger

```go
func WithSlogLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithSlogLogger sets the logger from an slog.Logger. Pass nil to restore the silent default.

#### func WithUsernameValidator

```go
func WithUsernameValidator(v UsernameValidator) Option
```

WithUsernameValidator registers a username/password validator called during ActivateSession when the client presents a UserNameIdentityToken. EnableAuthMode(ua.UserTokenTypeUserName) must also be called.

If no validator is registered the server rejects all username tokens with Bad\_UserAccessDenied: credentials nobody checks are not accepted. Compare passwords in constant time (crypto/subtle) or against a password hash.

#### func WithX509UserValidator

```go
func WithX509UserValidator(v X509UserValidator) Option
```

WithX509UserValidator registers a certificate validator called during ActivateSession when the client presents an X509IdentityToken. EnableAuthMode(ua.UserTokenTypeCertificate) must also be called.

If no validator is registered the server rejects all X.509 user tokens (the server still advertises the token type when the auth mode is enabled, but tokens cannot be activated without a configured validator).

### type PubReq

```go
type PubReq struct {
	// The data of the publish request
	Req *ua.PublishRequest

	// The request ID (from the header) of the publish request.  This has to be used when replying.
	ID uint32

	// Channel is the secure channel the Publish request arrived on. The
	// response has to be sent on the same channel: after a client reconnect
	// the session lives on a new channel, while the channel the subscription
	// was created on is gone.
	Channel *uasc.SecureChannel
}
```

### type PubSubAuthorizer

```go
type PubSubAuthorizer func(ctx context.Context, caller *MethodCaller, method string) ua.StatusCode
```

PubSubAuthorizer decides whether the caller of a PubSub configuration method (AddConnection, RemoveGroup, Enable, ...) may call it. method is the BrowseName of the method. It returns Good to allow the call or the Bad status to answer it with.

### type PushAuthorizer

```go
type PushAuthorizer func(ctx context.Context, caller *MethodCaller, method string) ua.StatusCode
```

PushAuthorizer decides whether the caller may call a certificate management method: the method name ("UpdateCertificate", "ApplyChanges", "OpenWithMasks", "AddCertificate", ...). It returns ua.StatusOK to allow the call, otherwise the status the call fails with (typically ua.StatusBadUserAccessDenied).

### type PushManagement

```go
type PushManagement struct {
	// TrustList is the trust list of the DefaultApplicationGroup the server
	// starts with (nil: an empty one, which rejects every client
	// certificate). It should hold the certificate, or the CA, of the
	// client that manages the server. SpecifiedLists is ignored: all four
	// lists are taken.
	TrustList *ua.TrustListDataType

	// HTTPSTrustList and UserTokenTrustList are the trust lists of the
	// DefaultHttpsGroup and the DefaultUserTokenGroup the server starts
	// with (nil: empty ones).
	HTTPSTrustList     *ua.TrustListDataType
	UserTokenTrustList *ua.TrustListDataType

	// HTTPSClientCertificates selects what the opc.https and opc.wss
	// endpoints do with TLS client certificates. The default leaves the
	// TLS configuration alone.
	HTTPSClientCertificates HTTPSClientAuth

	// MaxTrustListSize is the most bytes an encoded trust list may have,
	// published as MaxTrustListSize. Zero selects 1 MiB.
	MaxTrustListSize uint32

	// MaxRejectedCertificates bounds the list GetRejectedList returns: the
	// most recently rejected certificates. Zero selects 64.
	MaxRejectedCertificates int

	// ApplyImmediately makes every change take effect when its method
	// returns, without ApplyChanges: CloseAndUpdate and UpdateCertificate
	// then return applyChangesRequired false. By default changes are
	// collected in a transaction of the calling session and take effect
	// with ApplyChanges (Part 12 §7.10.2).
	ApplyImmediately bool

	// Authorizer decides who may call the certificate management methods
	// (nil: sessions with the SecurityAdmin role, Part 12 §7.2). Whatever it
	// decides, the methods are refused on channels that are not
	// SignAndEncrypt.
	Authorizer PushAuthorizer

	// Store, if set, persists what ApplyChanges and ResetToServerDefaults
	// apply. The server does not write files on its own. A Store that also
	// implements CertificateGroupStore persists the changes of every
	// certificate group; otherwise only those of the
	// DefaultApplicationGroup are persisted.
	Store CertificateStore

	// PFXPassword returns the password of a PKCS #12 (PFX) private key that
	// UpdateCertificate receives for the certificate group and type (Part
	// 12 §7.10.4 carries no password: it is a secret of the server). Nil
	// or an empty password reads PFX files without a password.
	PFXPassword func(ctx context.Context, certificateGroup, certificateType *ua.NodeID) (string, error)

	// TrustListUpdateFrequency is the UpdateFrequency of the trust lists
	// (Part 12 §7.8.2.1): how often they are expected to be updated. Zero
	// leaves it unset and the TrustListOutOfDate alarms inactive.
	TrustListUpdateFrequency time.Duration

	// Alarms, if set, adds the CertificateExpired and TrustListOutOfDate
	// alarms of the certificate groups (Part 12 §7.8.3).
	Alarms *CertificateAlarms

	// CertificateGroups are certificate groups of the application beyond
	// the three default ones (Part 12 §7.8.3: a CertificateGroupFolder may
	// hold more), for example a trust list for the certificates of a
	// third-party system or the client certificate of an outgoing
	// connection. Each is a CertificateGroupType object in the
	// CertificateGroups folder of ServerConfiguration with its own TrustList
	// and CertificateTypes, and takes part in the transactions,
	// GetCertificates, CreateSigningRequest, UpdateCertificate,
	// CreateSelfSignedCertificate, DeleteCertificate, ResetToServerDefaults
	// and the alarms like the default groups. The server does not use them
	// itself: the application reads them with Server.GroupCertificate and
	// validates against their trust lists with Server.VerifyGroupCertificate.
	CertificateGroups []CertificateGroup
}
```

PushManagement configures certificate management by the push model of OPC UA Part 12 §7: a client with the SecurityAdmin role manages the trust lists and the certificates of the server through the ServerConfiguration object (Part 12 §7.10.3).

The server has the three certificate groups of Part 12 §7.8.3:

  - DefaultApplicationGroup: the application instance certificates and the trust list the application certificates of the clients are validated against, which replaces WithClientCertificateTrustList.
  - DefaultHttpsGroup: the TLS certificate of the opc.https and opc.wss endpoints and the trust list for the TLS client certificates of HTTPSClientCertificates.
  - DefaultUserTokenGroup: the trust list X.509 user identity tokens are validated against, before a WithX509UserValidator is asked.

### type RBACAccessController

```go
type RBACAccessController struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RBACAccessController enforces OPC UA role-based access control by checking the node's RolePermissions against the session's assigned roles.

For each operation, it looks up the target node, retrieves its rolePermissions, and verifies that at least one of the session's roles has the required permission. If the node has no rolePermissions defined, the operation is allowed.

#### func NewRBACAccessController

```go
func NewRBACAccessController(srv *Server) *RBACAccessController
```

### type RegistrationEvent

```go
type RegistrationEvent struct {
	// DiscoveryServerURL is the URL given to [WithDiscoveryRegistration].
	DiscoveryServerURL string
	// Service is the service that was used last: "RegisterServer2" or
	// "RegisterServer".
	Service string
	// Online is true for a registration and false for the unregistration on
	// shutdown.
	Online bool
	// SecurityPolicyURI and SecurityMode are the security of the
	// SecureChannel that was used.
	SecurityPolicyURI string
	SecurityMode      ua.MessageSecurityMode
	// ConfigurationResults are the results the discovery server returned
	// for the discovery configurations of a RegisterServer2 request.
	ConfigurationResults []ua.StatusCode
	// Err is nil if the discovery server accepted the request.
	Err error
}
```

RegistrationEvent reports the outcome of one attempt to register with, or unregister from, a discovery server.

### type RegistrationOption

```go
type RegistrationOption func(*registrationConfig)
```

RegistrationOption configures the registration with a discovery server enabled with [WithDiscoveryRegistration](#func-withdiscoveryregistration).

#### func RegisterBackoff

```go
func RegisterBackoff(minDelay, maxDelay time.Duration) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterBackoff sets the delay before a failed registration is tried again: it starts at minDelay and doubles up to maxDelay. The defaults are one second and one minute.

#### func RegisterCertificateValidator

```go
func RegisterCertificateValidator(fn func(certDER []byte) error) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterCertificateValidator sets a function that decides whether the certificate of the discovery server (DER encoded) is trusted. It is called before a secured SecureChannel is opened; an error aborts the attempt. By default every certificate is accepted.

#### func RegisterDiscoveryURLs

```go
func RegisterDiscoveryURLs(urls ...string) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterDiscoveryURLs sets the discovery URLs to register instead of the server's endpoint URLs, e.g. the address under which the server is reachable from outside a container.

#### func RegisterEventHandler

```go
func RegisterEventHandler(fn func(RegistrationEvent)) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterEventHandler sets a function that is called after every attempt to register or unregister. It is called from the registration goroutine and must not block.

#### func RegisterInsecure

```go
func RegisterInsecure() RegistrationOption
```

RegisterInsecure allows the registration over a SecureChannel without security. A secured endpoint is still preferred if the server has a certificate and the discovery server offers one. Without this option a registration that cannot be secured fails.

#### func RegisterInterval

```go
func RegisterInterval(d time.Duration) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterInterval sets how often the registration is renewed. The default is DefaultRegisterInterval. Choose a value well below the registration timeout of the discovery server.

#### func RegisterMdnsServerName

```go
func RegisterMdnsServerName(name string) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterMdnsServerName sets the mDNS server name sent with RegisterServer2 (MdnsDiscoveryConfiguration). The default is the name set with [MulticastServerName](#func-multicastservername), or the application name.

#### func RegisterRequestTimeout

```go
func RegisterRequestTimeout(d time.Duration) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterRequestTimeout bounds one registration attempt, connecting included, and the unregistration on Close. The default is 10 seconds.

#### func RegisterSecurity

```go
func RegisterSecurity(policy string, mode ua.MessageSecurityMode) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterSecurity pins the security policy and mode of the SecureChannel to the discovery server instead of picking the most secure endpoint. policy is a policy URI or its short name ("Basic256Sha256").

#### func RegisterSemaphoreFile

```go
func RegisterSemaphoreFile(path string) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterSemaphoreFile sets the semaphore file path of the registration (Part 4 §5.4.5). The discovery server, which must be on the same machine, keeps the registration for as long as the file exists; the server is responsible for creating and deleting it.

#### func RegisterServerCapabilities

```go
func RegisterServerCapabilities(caps ...string) RegistrationOption
```

RegisterServerCapabilities sets the capability identifiers sent with RegisterServer2 (MdnsDiscoveryConfiguration). The default are the capabilities set with [MulticastCapabilities](#func-multicastcapabilities), or "NA".

### type Rejection

```go
type Rejection struct {
	// Service is the service the server refused: RejectedOpenSecureChannel
	// (e.g. an untrusted application certificate), RejectedCreateSession
	// or RejectedActivateSession (e.g. a wrong password).
	Service string
	// Status is the status the request was refused with.
	Status ua.StatusCode
	// RemoteAddr is the address of the client; nil over opc.https.
	RemoteAddr net.Addr
	// SecurityPolicyURI and SecurityMode are those of the secure channel;
	// for OpenSecureChannel those the client asked for.
	SecurityPolicyURI string
	SecurityMode      ua.MessageSecurityMode
	// ClientCertificate is the application instance certificate the client
	// sent, if any.
	ClientCertificate []byte
	// Session describes the session of a CreateSession (as far as the
	// request tells) or ActivateSession, with the identity type and user the
	// client tried; nil for OpenSecureChannel. The ID is nil when the
	// server knows no session.
	Session *SessionInfo
}
```

Rejection describes a request of a client that the server refused, for [SessionObserver.OnRejected](#func-sessionobserver-onrejected).

### type ReverseConnect

```go
type ReverseConnect struct {

	// kick wakes the connection loop when a connection ended: the client
	// may want a new one right away, and a slot became free.

	// done is closed when the connection loop has stopped and wg counts the
	// connections being served.

}
```

ReverseConnect is a reverse connect target: a client the server connects to. It is returned by [Server.AddReverseConnect](#func-server-addreverseconnect).

#### func (ReverseConnect) ClientURL

```go
func (rc *ReverseConnect) ClientURL() string
```

ClientURL returns the URL of the client the server connects to.

#### func (ReverseConnect) Close

```go
func (rc *ReverseConnect) Close() error
```

Close removes the target from the server: the server stops connecting to the client and closes the connections it opened to it, which ends the secure channels on them. Sessions and subscriptions are not deleted; they time out as after any other connection loss. Close is idempotent.

#### func (ReverseConnect) Connections

```go
func (rc *ReverseConnect) Connections() int
```

Connections returns the number of connections the client currently uses.

#### func (ReverseConnect) Err

```go
func (rc *ReverseConnect) Err() error
```

Err returns the reason the most recent connection attempt failed, or nil if it succeeded or none was made yet. A client that refuses the server (for example because it expects another ServerUri) shows up here.

#### func (ReverseConnect) State

```go
func (rc *ReverseConnect) State() ReverseConnectState
```

State returns the current state of the target.

### type ReverseConnectOption

```go
type ReverseConnectOption func(*reverseConnectConfig)
```

ReverseConnectOption configures a reverse connect target. See [WithReverseConnect](#func-withreverseconnect) and [Server.AddReverseConnect](#func-server-addreverseconnect).

#### func ReverseConnectEndpointURL

```go
func ReverseConnectEndpointURL(url string) ReverseConnectOption
```

ReverseConnectEndpointURL sets the EndpointUrl announced in the ReverseHello message: the URL of the endpoint the client is to use for the secure channel and the session. It defaults to the first endpoint of the server (see [EndPoint](#func-endpoint)).

#### func ReverseConnectMaxConnections

```go
func ReverseConnectMaxConnections(n int) ReverseConnectOption
```

ReverseConnectMaxConnections limits the number of connections the client may have in use at a time. While the limit is reached the server does not open another idle connection. A value that is not positive selects DefaultReverseConnectMaxConnections.

#### func ReverseConnectRetryInterval

```go
func ReverseConnectRetryInterval(initial, max time.Duration) ReverseConnectOption
```

ReverseConnectRetryInterval sets the delay before the first retry of a failed connection attempt and the upper bound the delay grows to as attempts keep failing (it doubles each time). Values that are not positive select the defaults, DefaultReverseConnectRetryInterval and DefaultReverseConnectMaxRetryInterval.

### type ReverseConnectState

```go
type ReverseConnectState int
```

ReverseConnectState is the state of a reverse connect target.

```go
const (
	// ReverseConnectConnecting: the server is opening a connection to the
	// client. This is also the state of a target whose server has not been
	// started yet.
	ReverseConnectConnecting ReverseConnectState = iota

	// ReverseConnectWaiting: a connection is open and announced with a
	// ReverseHello message; the client has not used it yet.
	ReverseConnectWaiting

	// ReverseConnectConnected: the client uses at least one connection.
	ReverseConnectConnected

	// ReverseConnectBackoff: the last attempt failed (see
	// [ReverseConnect.Err]) and the server waits before it tries again.
	ReverseConnectBackoff

	// ReverseConnectClosed: the target was removed or the server closed.
	ReverseConnectClosed
)
```

#### func (ReverseConnectState) String

```go
func (s ReverseConnectState) String() string
```

String returns the name of the state.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// nsView is the namespaces for readers that do not take mu (Node):
	// AddNamespace publishes a new slice, it never changes one in place.

	// opc.wss, nil without WebSocket endpoints
	// opc.https, nil without HTTPS endpoints
	// opc.wss with opcua+uajson, nil without EnableUAJSON

	// nextSecureChannelID uint32

	// Service Handlers are methods called to respond to service requests from clients
	// All services should have a method here.

	// methods stores registered server-side method handlers keyed by "objectID\x00methodID".

	SubscriptionService  *SubscriptionService
	MonitoredItemService *MonitoredItemService

	// eventItems tracks event-monitored-item filter state.

	// alarms holds the conditions (Part 9).

	// auditing tells whether the server reports audit events
	// (WithAuditing, SetAuditing).

	// histMu guards historian and historyCPs, which SetHistorian replaces
	// while services and event reports use them.

	// historian provides optional HistoryRead support (nil = unsupported).

	// historyCPs binds opaque HistoryRead continuation points to sessions.

	// histEventsAll marks the notifiers whose event history stores whole
	// events (EnableEventHistory without a filter), keyed by NodeID.String().

	// rcMu guards the reverse connect targets. rcCtx is the context of the
	// running server (nil before Start) and rcClosed is set by Close.

	// disc holds the discovery state: registered servers, the mDNS node and
	// the registration loops towards other discovery servers.

	// ps is the PubSub runtime and its information model (pubsub.go).

	// diag holds the server diagnostics (diagnostics.go).

	// push is the push certificate management (push.go), nil without
	// WithPushManagement.

}
```

Server is a high-level OPC-UA server.

It manages the full server lifecycle: listening for TCP connections, establishing secure channels, creating sessions, dispatching service requests to handlers, and managing subscriptions.

The server automatically populates namespace 0 with the standard OPC-UA address space. Custom namespaces can be added with [Server.AddNamespace](#func-server-addnamespace) or by creating a [NodeNameSpace](#type-nodenamespace) or [MapNamespace](#type-mapnamespace).

Create a Server with [New](#func-new), configure it with [Option](#type-option) functions, and start it with [Server.Start](#func-server-start). Call [Server.Close](#func-server-close) to shut down.

#### func New

```go
func New(opts ...Option) (*Server, error)
```

New creates and initializes a new OPC-UA server.

The server is configured with the given options. Namespace 0 is automatically populated with the standard OPC-UA node set, including Server status, capabilities, and current time nodes.

Call [Server.Start](#func-server-start) to begin accepting connections.

#### func (Server) AddAlarmGroup

```go
func (s *Server) AddAlarmGroup(cfg AlarmGroupConfig) (*AlarmGroup, error)
```

AddAlarmGroup creates an AlarmGroupType (or, with Suppression, AlarmSuppressionGroupType) object.

#### func (Server) AddAlarmMetrics

```go

```

AddAlarmMetrics creates an AlarmMetricsType object.

#### func (Server) AddCondition

```go
func (s *Server) AddCondition(cfg ConditionConfig) (*Condition, error)
```

AddCondition creates a condition instance (Part 9 §5.5) with the components of its type and the options of cfg, attaches it to its source node and returns it. The condition reports an initial event.

#### func (Server) AddNamespace

```go
func (s *Server) AddNamespace(ns NameSpace) int
```

AddNamespace registers a namespace with the server and assigns it a namespace index.

If the namespace is already registered, its existing index is returned. When the server already has 65536 namespaces, the most a UInt16 NamespaceIndex can address, the namespace is not registered, its ID is not set, an error is logged and AddNamespace returns -1. Use [NewNodeNameSpace](#func-newnodenamespace) or [NewMapNamespace](#func-newmapnamespace) which call this automatically.

#### func (Server) AddReverseConnect

```go
func (s *Server) AddReverseConnect(clientURL string, opts ...ReverseConnectOption) (*ReverseConnect, error)
```

AddReverseConnect makes the server open reverse connections to the client listening at clientURL ("opc.tcp://host:port").

The server connects to the client, announces itself with a ReverseHello message (carrying its ApplicationUri and the URL of the endpoint the client is to use) and waits for the client to open a secure channel on the connection. From then on the connection is served exactly like one the client had opened itself, with every security policy and service the server offers. As soon as the client uses a connection the server opens the next one, so that one idle connection is always available. An attempt that fails, because the client is not listening or refuses the server, is repeated with an increasing delay; a connection that breaks is replaced at once.

A target added before [Server.Start](#func-server-start) becomes active when the server starts. Targets are removed with [ReverseConnect.Close](#func-reverseconnect-close) and when the server closes.

#### func (Server) EnableEventHistory

```go
func (s *Server) EnableEventHistory(notifier *ua.NodeID, opts EventHistoryOptions) error
```

EnableEventHistory makes the Object or View notifier a HistoricalEventNode (Part 11 §5.4): it sets the SubscribeToEvents and HistoryRead bits of its EventNotifier attribute (and HistoryWrite with opts.Writable) and adds the HistoricalEventFilter Property. The events reported on the notifier from then on go to the [EventHistoryProvider](#type-eventhistoryprovider) of the server; the default [\*Historian](#type-historian) keeps them once EnableEvents was called for the notifier.

#### func (Server) EnableSecurityKeyPush

```go
func (s *Server) EnableSecurityKeyPush(rings *pubsubsec.KeyRings, opts ...SKSOption) error
```

EnableSecurityKeyPush makes the server a target of SetSecurityKeys (Part 14 §8.3.4, PublishSubscribe.SetSecurityKeys i=17364): an SKS pushes the keys of a SecurityGroup to the KeyRing registered in rings under its SecurityGroupId. Arguments: SecurityGroupId String, SecurityPolicyUri String, CurrentTokenId IntegerId, CurrentKey ByteString, FutureKeys ByteString\[], TimeToNextKey Duration, KeyLifetime Duration.

The method only runs over a SignAndEncrypt secure channel and for callers the SKSAuthorizer allows. Unknown groups are Bad\_NotFound, a policy other than the ring's Bad\_SecurityPolicyRejected and keys of the wrong length Bad\_SecurityChecksFailed (as open62541). Call it before Start.

#### func (Server) EnableSecurityKeyService

```go
func (s *Server) EnableSecurityKeyService(ks *pubsubsec.KeyService, opts ...SKSOption) (*SecurityKeyService, error)
```

EnableSecurityKeyService makes the server a Security Key Service (Part 14 §8) for the SecurityGroups of ks. It implements the methods of the standard PublishSubscribe object (i=14443):

  - GetSecurityKeys (i=15215): in SecurityGroupId String, StartingTokenId IntegerId, RequestedKeyCount UInt32; out SecurityPolicyUri String, FirstTokenId IntegerId, Keys ByteString\[], TimeToNextKey Duration, KeyLifetime Duration.
  - GetSecurityGroup (i=15440): in SecurityGroupId String; out SecurityGroupNodeId NodeId.
  - SecurityGroups.AddSecurityGroup (i=15444, and SecurityGroupFolderType AddSecurityGroup i=15461 on every SecurityGroupFolder): in SecurityGroupName String, KeyLifetime Duration, SecurityPolicyUri String, MaxFutureKeyCount UInt32, MaxPastKeyCount UInt32; out SecurityGroupId String, SecurityGroupNodeId NodeId.
  - SecurityGroups.RemoveSecurityGroup (i=15447, and i=15464 on every SecurityGroupFolder): in SecurityGroupNodeId NodeId.

Every SecurityGroup of ks gets a SecurityGroupType node below PublishSubscribe.SecurityGroups (or the SecurityGroupFolder of its SecurityGroupFolder path) with the properties SecurityGroupId, KeyLifetime, SecurityPolicyUri, MaxFutureKeyCount and MaxPastKeyCount; nodes follow groups added or removed later through ks.

The methods only run over a SignAndEncrypt secure channel (Bad\_SecurityModeInsufficient) and for callers the Authorizer of ks allows (Bad\_UserAccessDenied). Call it once, before Start.

#### func (Server) ReportAuditEvent

```go
func (s *Server) ReportAuditEvent(ctx context.Context, ev *BaseEvent, notifiers ...*ua.NodeID) bool
```

ReportAuditEvent reports an audit event (Part 5 §6.4.3) of an application method, for example one of the AuditUpdateMethodEventType subtypes a companion specification defines, when auditing is on ([WithAuditing](#func-withauditing)); it returns whether the event was reported.

The event goes to the event items of the Server object and of the notifiers given. Like the audit events of the server itself, only the sessions an [EventAccessController](#type-eventaccesscontroller) allows receive it. ReportAuditEvent sets what ev leaves unset: the EventId, the Time, the Severity (100) and the AuditEventType fields ActionTimeStamp, ServerId, ClientAuditEntryId and ClientUserId, the last two from the [MethodCaller](#type-methodcaller) of ctx. ev.Fields should carry Status and the fields of the event type. A subscription whose event queue is full is waited for a while (as for the events of conditions), so do not call it with a lock held that other calls need.

#### func (Server) ServeTrustList

```go
func (s *Server) ServeTrustList(obj *ua.NodeID, cfg TrustListConfig) (*TrustListObject, error)
```

ServeTrustList serves the TrustList object obj of the address space: an object of the TrustListType (Part 12 §7.8.2.1) whose methods and properties are its HasComponent and HasProperty children, for example a TrustList of a NodeSet that was imported. The methods are found by their BrowseName. It returns an error if obj or one of the methods Open, Read, Close and OpenWithMasks is missing.

Each handle of the file belongs to the session that opened it. A reader sees the trust list at the time of the Open; writes are kept until CloseAndUpdate.


#### func (Server) ServersOnNetwork

```go

```

ServersOnNetwork returns a copy of the ServerOnNetwork table in record id order: the server itself, the registered servers it announces and the servers discovered with mDNS. It is empty unless the server was created with [WithMulticastDiscovery](#func-withmulticastdiscovery) and is running.

#### func (Server) Session

```go

```


SetAuditing turns the audit events on or off.

#### func (Server) SetHistorian

```go
func (s *Server) SetHistorian(h HistoryProvider)
```

SetHistorian attaches a HistoryProvider for HistoryRead support. Pass nil to disable historical access (HistoryRead returns BadHistoryOperationUnsupported). A provider that also implements [EventHistoryProvider](#type-eventhistoryprovider) keeps the event history of the HistoricalEventNodes ([Server.EnableEventHistory](#func-server-enableeventhistory)). The HistoryServerCapabilities report what the provider supports.

#### func (Server) SetServerDiagnosticsEnabled

```go
func (s *Server) SetServerDiagnosticsEnabled(on bool)
```

SetServerDiagnosticsEnabled enables or disables the collection of diagnostics, as a write of Server.ServerDiagnostics.EnabledFlag does (Part 5 §6.3.3): enabling resets the diagnostics, disabling keeps them as they are. While disabled ServerDiagnosticsSummary keeps the values it had, the diagnostics arrays are empty and the sessions have no diagnostics objects.


Start initializes and starts a Server listening on addr If s was not initialized with NewServer(), addr defaults to localhost:0 to let the OS select a random port.

The opc.tcp endpoints come first, then the opc.wss and the opc.https ones.

#### func (Server) VerifyGroupCertificate

```go

```

VerifyGroupCertificate validates a certificate, or a certificate chain (concatenated DER, the certificate first), against the trust list of a certificate group. A rejected certificate goes to the list GetRejectedList returns. It is how the application uses the trust list of a group of PushManagement.CertificateGroups.

### type ServerMetrics

```go
type ServerMetrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called before invoking the service handler.
	// The service parameter is the OPC-UA service name (e.g. "Read", "Write",
	// "Browse", "Call", "CreateSubscription").
	OnRequest(service string)

	// OnResponse is called after the handler returns without error.
	OnResponse(service string, duration time.Duration)

	// OnError is called when the handler returns an error.
	OnError(service string, duration time.Duration, err error)
}
```

ServerMetrics receives callbacks for server-side OPC-UA service calls. All methods are called synchronously; implementations must be non-blocking (e.g. increment an atomic counter, send on a buffered channel).

Attach an implementation via [WithMetrics](#func-withmetrics).

### type Session

```go
type Session struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Session is the session a request came in on, as an [AccessController](#type-accesscontroller) sees it. It is read-only: it reports who the session is, not the secrets of the session (the AuthenticationToken, the nonces). A nil \*Session is a request without a session; its methods return zero values.

#### func (Session) ClientCertificate

```go
func (h *Session) ClientCertificate() []byte
```

ClientCertificate returns the application instance certificate (DER) the client sent in CreateSession; nil without one, and nil on a session with SecurityPolicy None, where the server ignores it (Part 4 §5.7.2.2).

#### func (Session) ID

```go
func (h *Session) ID() *ua.NodeID
```

ID returns the NodeId of the session (the SessionId of CreateSession).

#### func (Session) Identity

```go
func (h *Session) Identity() ua.IdentityToken
```

Identity returns the user identity token the session was activated with; nil before ActivateSession. The session does not keep the password of a UserNameIdentityToken: its Password is nil. The [RoleMapper](#type-rolemapper) gets the token with the password, decrypted.

#### func (Session) Roles

```go
func (h *Session) Roles() []*ua.NodeID
```

Roles returns the role NodeIds granted to the session (Part 18 §4.4). The slice is a copy.
