### type SessionInfo

```go
type SessionInfo struct {
	// ID is the SessionId (CreateSession).
	ID *ua.NodeID
	// Name is the SessionName the client chose (CreateSession).
	Name string
	// Client describes the client application (CreateSession
	// ClientDescription): ApplicationName, ApplicationURI, ProductURI.
	Client *ua.ApplicationDescription
	// EndpointURL is the endpoint the client asked for (CreateSession).
	EndpointURL string
	// RemoteAddr is the address of the client on the secure channel of the
	// last activation; nil over opc.https.
	RemoteAddr net.Addr
	// SecurityPolicyURI and SecurityMode are those of that secure channel.
	SecurityPolicyURI string
	SecurityMode      ua.MessageSecurityMode
	// IdentityType is the kind of user identity token of the last
	// activation, and User the user it names: the user name, the subject of
	// an X.509 user certificate, or empty (anonymous, issued token).
	IdentityType ua.UserTokenType
	User         string
	// Created is when the session was created, Activated when it was last
	// activated.
	Created   time.Time
	Activated time.Time
	// Reactivated is set for an ActivateSession of a session that was
	// activated before.
	Reactivated bool
}
```

SessionInfo describes a session for a [SessionObserver](#type-sessionobserver). Every call gets its own copy, which the observer may keep; ID is shared with the server and must not be modified.

### type SessionObserver

```go
type SessionObserver interface {
	// OnConnectionOpened is called when a client connection completed the
	// transport handshake (Hello/Acknowledge, Part 6 §7.1.3), for opc.tcp,
	// reverse and opc.wss connections. opc.https has no connections.
	OnConnectionOpened(remote net.Addr)

	// OnConnectionClosed is called when that connection ended, by either
	// side, after it was open for duration.
	OnConnectionClosed(remote net.Addr, duration time.Duration)

	// OnSessionActivated is called after a successful ActivateSession
	// (Part 4 §5.6.3), the first one of a session and every later one
	// (info.Reactivated), e.g. when the client moves the session to a new
	// secure channel after a reconnect.
	OnSessionActivated(info SessionInfo)

	// OnSessionClosed is called when an activated session ended. A session
	// that was created but never activated is not reported.
	OnSessionClosed(info SessionInfo, reason SessionCloseReason)

	// OnRejected is called when the server refused a client's
	// OpenSecureChannel (e.g. an untrusted application certificate),
	// CreateSession or ActivateSession (e.g. a wrong password or a token
	// type no endpoint offers). A request the server cannot decrypt or
	// verify is not reported.
	OnRejected(r Rejection)
}
```

SessionObserver is told about client connections and sessions as they begin and end, for logging and auditing in the application. Set it with [WithSessionObserver](#func-withsessionobserver).

The methods are called synchronously where the event happens: on the goroutine of the connection, or on the request dispatcher for the session events. The dispatcher handles the requests of all clients, so a session method that blocks holds up every client of the server, not only its own. They must not block; hand slow work to another goroutine. A panicking method is recovered and logged, and does not affect the connection or the session. Embed [BaseSessionObserver](#type-basesessionobserver) to implement only some of the methods.

### type Subscription

```go
type Subscription struct {
	Session                    *session
	ID                         uint32
	RevisedPublishingInterval  float64
	RevisedLifetimeCount       uint32
	RevisedMaxKeepAliveCount   uint32
	MaxNotificationsPerPublish uint32
	Priority                   uint8
	Channel                    *uasc.SecureChannel
	SequenceID                 uint32
	// seq is SequenceID for the goroutines other than run, which alone
	// changes SequenceID (TransferSubscriptions reads it).

	//SeqNums                   map[uint32]struct{}
	T *time.Ticker

	NotifyChannel      chan *ua.MonitoredItemNotification
	EventNotifyChannel chan *ua.EventFieldList
	ModifyChannel      chan *ua.ModifySubscriptionRequest

	// sentMessages stores the last N notification messages for retransmission via Republish.

	// the running flag and shutdown channel are used to signal the background task that it should stop.
	// multiple places can kill the subscription so make sure you check the running flag using the mutex
	// before closing the shutdown channel.
	Mu sync.Mutex

}
```

Subscription is the type that with its run function works in the background fulfilling subscription publishes.

MonitoredItems will send updates on the NotifyChannel to let the background task know that an event has occurred that needs to be published.

### type TrustListConfig

```go
type TrustListConfig struct {
	// Load returns the trust list the object serves (all four lists). It
	// is called for every Open, OpenWithMasks and change and must not
	// return nil.
	Load func() *ua.TrustListDataType

	// Authorize decides whether the caller may call a method of the object:
	// the method name ("Open", "OpenWithMasks", "Read", "Close",
	// "CloseAndUpdate", "AddCertificate", ...). write reports a call that
	// opens the file for writing or changes the trust list. It returns
	// ua.StatusOK to allow the call, otherwise the status the call fails
	// with. nil allows every call of a session.
	Authorize func(ctx context.Context, caller *MethodCaller, method string, write bool) ua.StatusCode

	// Update, if set, makes the trust list writable: it is called with the
	// complete new trust list (SpecifiedLists TrustListMasksAll) that
	// CloseAndUpdate, AddCertificate or RemoveCertificate made, after the
	// list was validated. The change takes effect when it returns
	// ua.StatusOK; CloseAndUpdate then reports applyChangesRequired false.
	// nil makes the object read-only: the writing methods return
	// Bad_NotWritable.
	Update func(ctx context.Context, caller *MethodCaller, tl *ua.TrustListDataType) ua.StatusCode

	// MaxSize is the most bytes the encoded trust list may have. Zero
	// selects 1 MiB.
	MaxSize uint32
}
```

TrustListConfig configures a TrustList object served by [Server.ServeTrustList](#func-server-servetrustlist).

### type X509UserValidator

```go
type X509UserValidator func(certDER []byte) error
```

X509UserValidator validates an X.509 identity token presented by a client during ActivateSession. The certificate is provided as DER-encoded bytes.

The server already verifies that the client holds the corresponding private key (via the UserTokenSignature). This callback is responsible for trust decisions: checking the certificate against a configured trust store, verifying revocation status, or applying application-specific policy.

Return nil to accept the certificate, or an error to reject it. ua.StatusBadIdentityTokenRejected and ua.StatusBadUserAccessDenied are the appropriate status codes for policy-based rejection.
